newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends up on trade buying, some covering.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends up on trade buying, some covering.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed up at session highs on Wednesday, boosted by trade buying and light short-covering.
May ended up 12 stg at 1,018 stg per tonne and July jumped 14 to 1,038. Total volume stood at 6,419 contracts, with July grabbing 2,862.
Traders said trade buying emerged to lift prices in the morning, with one large trade house said to have bought a few hundred July contracts.
In the afternoon, buying resumed with prices getting an added boost by scattered buying in hundred-lots in New York.
Some traders also said late short-covering helped push prices higher.
Switches were active, most notably in May/July and July/September.
Light arbitrage against New York was also seen as some expected the spread to widen, with London commanding a higher premium, some traders said.
Some traders said the market was still benefitting from talk that shippers were having difficulty fulfilling their committments.
That talk was also keeping July and September at premiums to December, traders said. At the close, July was 11 stg and September was 23 stg higher than December.
Technically, July cocoa traded an outside day, falling below Tuesday's low early but then recovering to score the week's high.
But some analysts were not yet convinced that cocoa has resumed its uptrend. They said cocoa still needed to pierce resistance near 1,045 by the end of the week before looking higher.
Others said they would feel more confident in the upmove if outright volume was higher. Traders attributed most of the day's volume to switches.
In options, 33 July 1,100 stg calls and 20 July 1,200 stg calls changed hands.
